notes: Imported verbatim from https://github.com/Amey-Thakur/CLAUDE-CERTIFICATIONS (MIT). Sub-skills were resolved from each question's domain label, so attribution within a domain is indicative. Single-answer, four-option items only.

questions.stem: A service sends the same 8,000-token system prompt on every request and cost is dominated by input tokens. What is the first change to evaluate?

options.text: Rewriting the system prompt to be shorter
options.rationale: Shortening sacrifices capability, a cheaper model trades quality, and fewer requests changes the product

options.text: Switching to a cheaper model
options.rationale: Shortening sacrifices capability, a cheaper model trades quality, and fewer requests changes the product

options.text: Caching the stable prefix so it is not reprocessed on every call
options.rationale: A large unchanging prefix repeated per call is what caching addresses, without losing any instruction.

options.text: Reducing the number of requests
options.rationale: Shortening sacrifices capability, a cheaper model trades quality, and fewer requests changes the product

questions.stem: An endpoint must return within 500 ms but the model needs longer for a good answer. What is the appropriate pattern?

options.text: Return an acknowledgement immediately and deliver the result through a callback or poll
options.rationale: Decoupling acceptance from completion satisfies the latency contract without degrading the answer.

options.text: Truncate the model's output
options.rationale: Truncation and a minimal model sacrifice the result, and the timeout is the stated constraint

options.text: Use the smallest model regardless of quality
options.rationale: Truncation and a minimal model sacrifice the result, and the timeout is the stated constraint

options.text: Increase the timeout on the client
options.rationale: Truncation and a minimal model sacrifice the result, and the timeout is the stated constraint

questions.stem: What does a stop reason indicating the maximum token limit tell you?

options.text: The input was too long
options.rationale: An oversized input fails before generation, and neither a malformed request nor a refusal produces this reason

options.text: The request was malformed
options.rationale: An oversized input fails before generation, and neither a malformed request nor a refusal produces this reason

options.text: The model refused the request
options.rationale: An oversized input fails before generation, and neither a malformed request nor a refusal produces this reason

options.text: The output was cut off before the model finished
options.rationale: That stop reason reports that generation hit the output ceiling.

questions.stem: A tool result returns 50,000 tokens of JSON, most of it unused. What is the right fix?

options.text: Raise the model's context limit
options.rationale: A larger window delays the problem, a second call adds cost and failure surface, and calling less often does not change the payload

options.text: Change the tool to return only the fields the task needs
options.rationale: Tools should return what the task requires, which preserves context for reasoning.

options.text: Summarise the JSON with a second model call
options.rationale: A larger window delays the problem, a second call adds cost and failure surface, and calling less often does not change the payload

options.text: Call the tool less frequently
options.rationale: A larger window delays the problem, a second call adds cost and failure surface, and calling less often does not change the payload

questions.stem: Which condition warrants a retry with backoff rather than surfacing an error?

options.text: The request contained an invalid parameter
options.rationale: An invalid parameter will fail identically, and disagreement or length are not transport failures

options.text: The service returned a rate limit or a transient server error
options.rationale: Rate limits and transient server errors are the recoverable class.

options.text: The model returned an answer you disagree with
options.rationale: An invalid parameter will fail identically, and disagreement or length are not transport failures

options.text: The response exceeded the expected length
options.rationale: An invalid parameter will fail identically, and disagreement or length are not transport failures

questions.stem: A workload runs nightly over 50,000 records with no interactive requirement. Which choice reduces cost most?

options.text: Streaming each request
options.rationale: Streaming serves interactive use, the largest model raises cost, and concurrency does not change unit price

options.text: Using the largest model for accuracy
options.rationale: Streaming serves interactive use, the largest model raises cost, and concurrency does not change unit price

options.text: Increasing concurrency against the standard endpoint
options.rationale: Streaming serves interactive use, the largest model raises cost, and concurrency does not change unit price

options.text: Submitting the work as a batch
options.rationale: Large, uniform, latency-tolerant work is exactly the batch case, and it is materially cheaper.

questions.stem: Accuracy on a simple extraction task is identical between a small and a large model. What should be deployed?

options.text: The small model, since it meets the requirement at lower cost
options.rationale: Where the requirement is met, the cheaper option is correct, and changing inputs are handled by re-evaluating.

options.text: The large model, in case inputs change
options.rationale: Insurance against hypothetical change, alternation, and recency all spend without benefit

options.text: Both, alternating between them
options.rationale: Insurance against hypothetical change, alternation, and recency all spend without benefit

options.text: The newest model available
options.rationale: Insurance against hypothetical change, alternation, and recency all spend without benefit

questions.stem: A task requires the model to plan across many interacting constraints and revise as it goes. What does this argue for?

options.text: The smallest model, to keep cost down
options.rationale: A small model and splitting both fragment the reasoning, and prompt length does not add capability

options.text: Splitting the task across several small models
options.rationale: A small model and splitting both fragment the reasoning, and prompt length does not add capability

options.text: A more capable model, since the work is reasoning-heavy
options.rationale: Multi-step reasoning under interacting constraints is where capability differences show.

options.text: A longer prompt with the same model
options.rationale: A small model and splitting both fragment the reasoning, and prompt length does not add capability

questions.stem: An agent is given ten tools, three of which overlap in purpose. What is the likely consequence?

options.text: Faster execution, since more options are available
options.rationale: Overlap does not improve speed, reduce cost, or help error handling

options.text: Lower token cost
options.rationale: Overlap does not improve speed, reduce cost, or help error handling

options.text: Better error handling
options.rationale: Overlap does not improve speed, reduce cost, or help error handling

options.text: More frequent wrong tool selection
options.rationale: Overlapping tools make selection ambiguous, which is where agents go wrong.

questions.stem: What should terminate an agent loop?

options.text: A fixed wall-clock timeout only
options.rationale: A timeout alone does not recognize success, the model's own judgment is not a guarantee, and exhausting context is a failure rather than a termination

options.text: The model deciding it is finished
options.rationale: A timeout alone does not recognize success, the model's own judgment is not a guarantee, and exhausting context is a failure rather than a termination

options.text: An explicit success condition, with a step ceiling as a backstop
options.rationale: A defined success condition ends the loop correctly, and the ceiling bounds the failure case.

options.text: Running out of context
options.rationale: A timeout alone does not recognize success, the model's own judgment is not a guarantee, and exhausting context is a failure rather than a termination

questions.stem: Where should a stable instruction that must apply to every turn be placed?

options.text: At the end of the latest user message
In the system prompt
options.rationale: The system prompt is designed for persistent framing across the exchange.

options.text: Repeated in each user message
In a tool description
options.rationale: Placing it in user turns (A, C) mixes configuration with input, and tool descriptions govern tool selection

questions.stem: Which change most improves output that is correct but inconsistently formatted?

options.text: Providing an example of the exact output required
options.rationale: An example defines the target unambiguously, which is what formatting consistency needs.

options.text: Raising the temperature
options.rationale: Higher temperature increases variance, a vague adjective does not specify, and a larger model does not know your format

options.text: Asking for the output to be neat
options.rationale: Higher temperature increases variance, a vague adjective does not specify, and a larger model does not know your format

options.text: Using a larger model
options.rationale: Higher temperature increases variance, a vague adjective does not specify, and a larger model does not know your format

questions.stem: What is the most important property of a tool description?

options.text: It states what the tool does, when to use it, and what each parameter means
options.rationale: The description is the model's only basis for choosing and calling the tool correctly.

options.text: It is short
options.rationale: Brevity is secondary to clarity, and implementation detail and naming do not guide selection

options.text: It lists the implementation language
options.rationale: Brevity is secondary to clarity, and implementation detail and naming do not guide selection

options.text: It matches the function name exactly
options.rationale: Brevity is secondary to clarity, and implementation detail and naming do not guide selection

questions.stem: Content retrieved from an external site contains instructions aimed at the model. What is the correct defense?

options.text: Instruct the model in the system prompt to ignore such content
options.rationale: Prompt instructions and phrase filters are bypassable, and context size is irrelevant

options.text: Treat retrieved content as untrusted data and bound the model's permissions outside the prompt
options.rationale: The durable control is that the model cannot exceed its granted permissions regardless of what the content says.

options.text: Scan for known injection phrases and block them
options.rationale: Prompt instructions and phrase filters are bypassable, and context size is irrelevant

options.text: Use a model with a larger context window
options.rationale: Prompt instructions and phrase filters are bypassable, and context size is irrelevant

questions.stem: A prompt change improved results on the five examples you tested. What should happen before it reaches production?

options.text: Ship it, since all five improved
Ask the model to compare the two prompts
options.rationale: Self-comparison is not measurement, and shipping first (A, D) makes users the test

options.text: Evaluate it against a held-out set that reflects real inputs, on defined criteria
options.rationale: Five hand-picked cases cannot separate a real gain from noise, which is what an evaluation set settles.

options.text: Ship it to a small percentage of traffic and watch error rates
